focus: Bot computer design beyond a worktree: what a terminal genuinely cannot give, and the smallest addition that closes the gap, given that skilled bots already keeps a per-run folder with retention and that only two executor kinds give an OS-level sandbox
noveltyJustification: 7 of 11 findings are new code facts (the run-folder path and its two refusals, the 200-run retention, the three-kind preventive-sandbox map, the opencode and devin comments, the worktree link rule) and 4 restate prior evidence or draw the design conclusion; a 0.10 simplicity bonus applies because the answer collapses the container question to a working directory and a documented command.
ruledOut: a per-bot container (it exists to serve a browser farm, and a small team runs one bot at a time)
gVisor (OpenBot leaves it unset by default and the executor kinds that matter already give an OS boundary)
a profiles volume (the operator's own browser profile already is one)

label: Skilled bots already keeps a per-run folder at <skilledTree>/.skilled/skills/.state/system-skilled-bots/<identity>/runs/<runId>, created owner-only at mode 0700.

The run folder is refused when the Skilled tree is a linked worktree because worktree cleanup would delete the evidence, and refused when the path is not gitignored so a vendored tree never puts run files in its git status.
The run folder is retained per bot at 200 runs, and the reaper keeps any run folder whose needs-you item is still open or awaiting resume.

The workspace volume OpenBot gets from agent-workspace:/workspace already exists in skilled bots as the run folder; the gap is that the run folder is treated as evidence and never as a working directory the bot is told about.

The sandbox is not a container: EXECUTOR_PREVENTIVE_SANDBOX_CAPABILITY is true for only cli-codex, cli-cursor and cli-deepseek-harness, and every other kind's sandbox is a tool gate or an approval mode.
The cli-opencode comment states the exact limit: workspace-write denies external_directory to the file tools only, and Bash can still write outside the working directory.
cli-devin never passes --sandbox at all, because confinement there is the fan-out's post-hoc write-containment guard rather than an OS boundary.

The worktree is a tree of the repo and not a home: it links the launcher's shared paths instead of a full install so setup needs no network, and removal unlinks each recorded link as a link and never follows it.

OpenBot's computer gives three things a worktree cannot: a headed browser on its own X server, profiles that survive restarts, and a shell whose environment is the container's rather than the server's.
Of those three only the browser is genuinely unavailable to a terminal, and it is unavailable for a stated reason: bot checks such as Cloudflare's challenge treat headless worse.

The smallest addition is not a container but two small things: telling the bot its run folder and starting its shell there, and an opt-in headed browser behind one command rather than a per-bot computer.

reason: it is the largest piece of OpenBot's computer and exists to serve a browser farm, while a small team runs one bot at a time on one machine
OpenBot itself leaves it unset by default, and the executor kinds that matter already give an OS boundary
the operator's own browser profile is the profiles volume and is already logged in
